# Draft:Crimean-Nogai war (1507-1511)

Crimean-Nogai War (1507-1511)
The Crimean-Nogai War (1507-1511) — armed conflict between the Crimean Khanate, led by Mengli Giray, and the Nogai Horde with Astrakhan Khanate, led by Agish-biy, Said-Ahmed, Abd al-Kerim and other Nogai murzas.
The 1st Nogai Campaign to Crimea
In 1507, the Crimean army, led by Mengli Giray was preparing to march on the Tsardom of Moscow as per an agreement between the Khan and Sigismund I. Upon learning of the departure of the Khan's main forces, the Nogais launched an attack on the Crimean Khanate. On the orders of Mengli Giray, the army, led by Kalga Mehmed Giray, turned towards the Nogais. After one skirmish, the enemy turned back home. The attack was repelled.
The 2nd Nogai Campaign to Crimea
Two years after the first attack on Crimea, the Nogais, in 1509, led by Agish-biy, Said-Ahmed and Abd al-Karim, again attacked the Crimean possessions. Mehmed Giray, with an army of 250,000, utterly defeated the Nogai army
Crimean Campaign against the Nogais
In 1510, Mengli Giray set out on a campaign against the Nogais, supposedly to take revenge on them for the previous year's defeat and the loss of two sons. Having crossed the Don River, the khan encountered the Nogais, who were unprepared for battle. After defeating them twice, he took 70,000 captive.
The 3rd Nogai Campaign against Crimea
In 1511, while the Crimean army was on campaign against Wallachia, Said-Ahmed, uniting with Mamai-biy, raided the Crimean Khanate.  Having approached Perekop and taken prisoners, the Nogais hastily retreated.
